# Salvage Specialist
Salvage Specialists are responsible for the undertaking of expeditions and wreck salvaging around the station space.
1. You report directly to the [color=#ffe100]Quartermaster[/color] and should communicate with the Quartermaster before and after each expedition with a verbal status report. After every 2 expeditions or if the salvage crew must return sooner, a [color=#ffe100]formal docking procedure[/color] must be completed.
This procedure is as follows: - The salvage team will notify the Quartermaster of their intent to return to the station. - Any contraband found is to be turned over to Security. Contraband request forms may be filled out for these items. - Security will not approve highly illegal contraband. [color=#ffe100]Faxes to Central Command[/color] should be prepared for these items instead. - Any salvage materials found should be processed and then delivered or sold. - Any damage to the ship/crew should be reported and repaired.
2. Highly dangerous expeditions may only be undertaken with the express permission of the Quartermaster. Going on unauthorized expeditions is grounds for demotion.
3. Unpermitted contraband found while on an expedition may [color=#ff0000]not[/color] be used without a valid permit. Exceptions for imminent loss of life or grievous bodily harm are accepted.
4. Upon arriving aboard the station, all unpermitted contraband [color=#ff0000]must[/color] be delivered to the Security department immediately.
6. Salvage Specialists are to follow the guidelines for Cargo Technicians when on station. Salvage Specialists are [color=#ff0000]not[/color] to visibly carry weaponry or contraband equipment without prior authorisation from the Quartermaster, Head of Security, or Captain.
7. Machinery may [color=#ff0000]not[/color] be moved from the station to the shuttle unless there are duplicates available on station. Equipment like ore processors and the salvage ticket machine are for use by both Salvage Specialists and Mining Specialists, removal impedes Mining Specialists duties.
8. The Ticket Vendors are [color=#ff0000]not[/color] to be modified or moved from their positions aboard the station unless significant structural damage has been sustained and the vendors are at risk of total destruction.
## Deputisation In dire circumstances, the Captain or Head of Security may authorise salvagers to act as additional fighters in an ongoing conflict aboard the station. Salvagers are deputised by default on [color=#8d281e]Code Delta[/color]. [color=#ff0000]Salvagers may not act as Security personnel in any capacity outside of explicit deputisation[/color]. This subsection will cover the details of this process.
1. Deputised Salvagers have all the permissions and privileges of station Security personnel, and are held to the same standard in case of abuse of power.
2. Deputised Salvagers may openly bear arms and wear permitted equipment. Deputised Salvagers may use lethal force within any reasonable circumstance.
3. Deputised Salvagers answer to the Captain, Head of Security, Warden, and Quartermaster in that order. Salvagers who accept deputisation are expected to directly assist with station defense.
